ei.title: Chapter 4-10 1번: The Flexible Boundaries of Social Bonds
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have (A)[evolved / declined] to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather (B)[flexible / rigid]. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as (C)[distinct / similar] from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 우리의 복잡한 뇌는 진화했고(evolved), 사회 집단의 정의는 유연하며(flexible), 동물을 인간과 구별된다고(distinct) 본다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① evolved — flexible — similar (C 반대: 구별된→비슷한)
❌ ② declined — flexible — distinct (A 반대: 진화하다→쇠퇴하다)
✅ ③ evolved — flexible — distinct — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ evolved — rigid — distinct (B 반대: 유연한→경직된)

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can (A)[relate / ignore] to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a (B)[deceased / living] loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still (C)[attribute / deny] certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 반려동물의 욕구에 공감할 수 있다고(relate) 믿고, 고인의(deceased) 유골을 가까이 두며, 인간적 특성을 부여한다(attribute).
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignore — deceased — attribute (A 반대: 공감하다→무시하다)
✅ ② relate — deceased — attribute — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ relate — living — attribute (B 반대: 고인의→살아있는)
❌ ④ relate — deceased — deny (C 반대: 부여하다→부정하다)

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have evolved to (A)[establish / sever] strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if (B)[inanimate / living] objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute (C)[certain / random] human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 강한 사회적 유대를 형성하기(establish) 위해, 무생물(inanimate) 대상이 뚜렷한 성격이 없더라도, 특정한(certain) 인간적 특성을 부여한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① sever — inanimate — certain (A 반대: 형성하다→단절하다)
❌ ② establish — living — certain (B 반대: 무생물→살아있는)
❌ ③ establish — inanimate — random (C 반대: 특정한→무작위의)
✅ ④ establish — inanimate — certain — 원문 일치 ←정답

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have ①<u>evolved</u> to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather ②<u>fixed</u>. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can ③<u>relate</u> to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct ④<u>personality</u>, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '고정된(fixed)'이 아니라 '유연한(flexible)'이 문맥상 적절하다. 사회 집단의 범위를 정의하는 것은 상당히 유연해 보인다.
det.analysis:
① evolved — 진화하다, 원문 일치
② fixed — 원문은 flexible(유연한) ←정답
③ relate — 공감하다, 원문 일치
④ personality — 성격, 원문 일치

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social ①<u>bonds</u>, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, ②<u>desires</u>, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their ③<u>existence</u>. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still ④<u>remove</u> certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '제거하다(remove)'가 아니라 '부여하다(attribute)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 인간적 특성을 비인간 대상에 부여한다.
det.analysis:
① bonds — 유대, 원문 일치
② desires — 욕구, 원문 일치
③ existence — 존재, 원문 일치
④ remove — 원문은 attribute(부여하다) ←정답

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one ①<u>apart</u>, believing those ashes ②<u>continue</u> to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human ③<u>characteristics</u> to non-human objects or ④<u>beings</u>, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '떨어져서(apart)'가 아니라 '가까이에(nearby)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 고인의 유골을 가까이에 둔다.
det.analysis:
① apart — 원문은 nearby(가까이에) ←정답
② continue — 계속하다, 원문 일치
③ characteristics — 특성, 원문 일치
④ beings — 존재(들), 원문 일치

det.korean: 특정한 인간적 특성(characteristics)을 비인간 대상에 부여한다.
det.analysis:

det.korean: 유골이 그들의 존재(existence)에 대한 연결고리 역할을 계속한다고 믿는다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① personality — 성격 (무생물에 관한 뒷문장 개념)
❌ ② family — 가족 (존재가 아닌 관계)
❌ ③ link — 연결고리 (바로 앞에 나옴, some link to their ___)
✅ ④ existence — 존재 ←정답
det.tip: some link to their existence = 그들의 존재에 대한 어떤 연결

det.korean: evolved = 진화하다 → developed(발전하다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① declined — 쇠퇴하다 (반의어)
✅ ② developed — 발전하다 ←정답
❌ ③ remained — 남아있다 (변화 없음의 의미)
❌ ④ vanished — 사라지다 (의미축 다름)

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 attribute의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: attribute = ~에 부여하다/돌리다 → assign(부여하다, 할당하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① assign — 부여하다, 할당하다 ←정답
❌ ② deny — 부정하다 (부여의 반대)
❌ ③ discover — 발견하다 (의미축 다름)
❌ ④ remove — 제거하다 (부여의 반대)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 distinct의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: distinct = 구별되는 → separate(별개의, 분리된)
det.analysis:
❌ ① identical — 동일한 (반의어)
❌ ② common — 흔한, 공통의 (의미축 다름)
❌ ③ familiar — 친숙한 (구별과 관련 없음)
✅ ④ separate — 별개의 ←정답

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 complex의 의미와 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: complex(복잡한) ↔ straightforward(단순한, 간단한)
det.analysis:
❌ ① advanced — 발전된 (의미축 다름)
❌ ② elaborate — 정교한 (동의어 방향)
✅ ③ straightforward — 단순한, 간단한 ←정답
❌ ④ detailed — 상세한 (의미축 다름)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 inanimate의 의미와 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: inanimate(무생물의, 생명이 없는) ↔ sentient(감각이 있는, 의식이 있는)
det.analysis:
❌ ① artificial — 인공적인 (의미축 다름, 자연 vs 인공)
✅ ② sentient — 감각이 있는, 의식이 있는 ←정답
❌ ③ motionless — 움직이지 않는 (동의어 방향)
❌ ④ abstract — 추상적인 (의미축 다름)

questions.passage:
(A) Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to <u>serve</u> as some link to their existence.

(B) The waiter was ready to <u>serve</u> the guests their dinner at the banquet.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 serve의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 유골이 존재와의 연결고리 역할을 하다(function as) / (B) 손님에게 저녁을 제공하다(provide/bring food)
det.analysis:
✅ ① 역할을 하다 — 제공하다 ←정답
❌ ② 제공하다 — 역할을 하다 (의미 뒤바뀜)
❌ ③ 봉사하다 — 대접하다 (A는 봉사가 아닌 기능/역할)
❌ ④ 역할을 하다 — 봉사하다 (B는 봉사가 아닌 음식 제공)
det.tip: serve: (A) 역할을 하다(function as) vs (B) 제공하다(provide food/service)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to regard something as being caused by or belonging to a particular person or thing"

det.korean: 어떤 것을 특정 사람이나 사물에 의해 야기된 것으로 간주하거나 속하는 것으로 여기다 → attribute(부여하다, ~의 탓으로 돌리다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① establish — 설립하다, 형성하다 (원인 귀속이 아님)
❌ ② relate — 관련짓다, 공감하다 (귀속이 아닌 연관)
✅ ③ attribute — 부여하다, ~의 탓으로 돌리다 ←정답
❌ ④ define — 정의하다 (규정하는 것이지 귀속이 아님)

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but __________ (define) what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 사회 집단에 속해야 할 것을 정의하는 것(defining)은 상당히 유연해 보인다 → define(동사원형) → defining(동명사, 주어 역할)
det.analysis: __________ (define) what should be part of → 주어 자리 동명사 → defining. define(정의하다, 동사원형)을 defining(동명사)로 변환. 주어 역할을 하는 동명사.

questions.passage: Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct __________ (personal), many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 무생물이 뚜렷한 성격(personality)을 가지고 있지 않더라도 → personal(형용사) → personality(명사)
det.analysis: a distinct __________ (personal) → 관사 a + 형용사 distinct 뒤 명사 자리 → personality. personal(개인의, 형용사)을 personality(성격, 명사)로 변환.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 사람들은 반려동물을 마치 가족 구성원인 것처럼(as if they are members of their family) 대한다.
det.analysis:

❌ ③ as if they are wild animals — 야생동물인 것처럼 (반려동물과 정반대)
❌ ④ as if they can survive alone — 혼자 생존 가능한 것처럼 (문맥 무관)

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as __________. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.

det.analysis:
❌ ① a direct path to their dreams — 꿈으로의 직접적 경로 (유골과 무관)

✅ ③ some link to their existence — 그들의 존재에 대한 어떤 연결 ←정답
❌ ④ a distinct personality of theirs — 뚜렷한 성격 (뒷문장에서 무생물에 성격이 없다고 함)
